readers.who: Independent developers (one or two people) building consumer-facing mobile apps who are responsible for product, code, and ops.
readers.knows: Comfortable with end-to-end product development: mobile and backend stacks, trade-offs, and pragmatic engineering; not specialists in physiotherapy.
readers.label: Solo product devs
readers.wants: Post‑mortems of decisions, concrete technical trade‑offs, performance numbers, what broke and why, and enough context to copy or avoid the same mistakes; they should come away able to reuse code ideas or architecture patterns.
readers.stopsFor: Clear technical diagrams, measured results (latency, error rates, accuracy), concrete code snippets, and concise “what we would change” bullets.
readers.turnsOff: Overly high-level marketing language, vague commitments, hand‑wavy ML claims, and long clinical explanations unrelated to engineering.

readers.who: Engineers focused on computer vision or machine learning, often contributors or contractors, who want to understand pose estimation, model choices, and evaluation.
readers.knows: They know pose estimation models, metrics (precision/recall, F1, AUC), data annotation issues, and model deployment constraints on mobile or serverless infra.
readers.label: CV / ML engineers
readers.wants: Architecture of the pose pipeline, model sizes and inference times, sample failure cases, dataset and annotation practices, and reproducible benchmarks to compare with their own work.
readers.stopsFor: Quantified model evaluations, dataset descriptions, code or model checkpoints, and examples of edge cases with visuals.
readers.turnsOff: Vague accuracy claims, missing evaluation methodology, lack of reproducible steps, or anonymized/noisy data descriptions.

readers.who: Engineers responsible for APIs, scaling, privacy, and deployment who read the repo to learn operational and architectural decisions for similar small teams.
readers.knows: Experienced with REST/gRPC APIs, database schemas, monitoring, CI/CD, k8s or serverless, GDPR/privacy basics; they value operational simplicity for small teams.
readers.label: Backend / infra engineers
readers.wants: Clear API contracts, data retention and privacy tradeoffs, deployment steps, monitoring/SLIs, cost estimates, and failure recovery patterns they can adapt.
readers.stopsFor: Clear diagrams of data flow, schema examples, deployment scripts, and cost/perf numbers.
readers.turnsOff: Undocumented APIs, missing privacy justification, hand‑wavy scaling claims, or opaque stateful architectures.

readerPortrait.basedOnAudience: Des développeurs qui construisent des produits seuls ou à deux : ils veulent voir les arbitrages techniques, ce qui a cassé, les chiffres de perf et les décisions d'architecture. Pas des kinés.
